pr_title: LE Audio: Unicast client release fix
pr_body:
Fixes an issue with releasing a stream as the unicast client. 

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/56110

issue_context.title: LE Audio: BAP Unicast Client cannot release stream if server caches
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
If we as the unicast client call `bt_bap_stream_release`, but the unicast server caches the ASE, then we never go into the idle state and the `bt_bap_stream_ops.released` callback is never called. Even if we call `bt_bap_stream_release` again for the same stream, it may just go into the codec configured state again. 

**To Reproduce**
N/A

**Expected behavior**
When calling `bt_bap_stream_release` we should, unless rejected by the server, consider the state change into codec configured the same way we do for the idle state, i.e. cleanup everything and call the `released` callback. 

**Impact**
If a unicast server caches the codec configuration, we will never be able to release a stream, which can be a showstopper as the only way out of this state is an ACL disconnect. 

**Logs and console output**
N/A

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Commit SHA or Version used: 82efb21e91a241d62608d5dd841fcadfc6afef96

**Additional context**
In the BAP unicast client implementation we already have the `release_requested` boolean which we should be able to utilize to handle state transitions into the codec configured state properly. 
Ideally it would something as simple as
```
if (release_requested) {
    consider stream released
} else {
    consider stream to be in codec configured state
}
```

review_comments:
Nice catch - I had wrongly expected the `struct bt_bap_unicast_client_ep` to be memset on reset, but it only resets a few fields. 

Added initialization of `release_requested` and `cp_ntf_pending`
